output.title: Decreasing students’ stress through time management training

scenes.narration: University students often feel stressed, and this paper asks whether a short time management training can change that in higher education.
scenes.layout_description: A student sits beside a messy clock and notebook while a simple arrow points toward a calmer scene.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimalist hand-drawn student at a desk with scattered papers, a clock, and an orange arrow toward a tidier desk; cream background, black ink, orange and yellow highlights.

scenes.narration: The authors studied perceived control of time, perceived stress, and demands, using demands as a control variable that should not change.
scenes.layout_description: Three labeled circles are arranged side by side, with the control variable visually separated.
scenes.visual_prompt: Three simple icons: a steering wheel for control of time, a wavy stress line, and a stack of duties for demands; one icon highlighted in orange as the control variable.

scenes.narration: Twenty-three undergraduate students completed the main analysis, after attending a four hour training and answering questionnaires before, two weeks after, and four weeks after.
scenes.layout_description: A small timeline runs across the slide with three check marks and a training block in the middle.
scenes.visual_prompt: A clean timeline with a training box labeled by hand, three small student figures, and check marks at pretest, 2 weeks, and 4 weeks.

scenes.narration: The study used a non-equivalent dependent variable design, meaning one group was trained and a variable that should not change was also measured.
scenes.layout_description: One group of students stands under a training banner, while a separate neutral icon sits below as the unchanged measure.
scenes.visual_prompt: A simple diagram of one student group receiving a toolbox labeled training, with a separate untouched clipboard labeled control variable.

scenes.narration: The training focused on prioritizing, goal setting, strategy development, daily planning, and monitoring, all meant to support better time management.
scenes.layout_description: Five small action icons form a loose circle around a central clock.
scenes.visual_prompt: Clock surrounded by hand-drawn icons for list sorting, target, path, calendar, and checkmark, with orange and yellow accents.

scenes.narration: Students reflected on their activities, chose important goals, planned steps, anticipated obstacles, and made concrete schedules for their studies.
scenes.layout_description: A student writes a plan that moves from left to right in simple boxes.
scenes.visual_prompt: Student at desk connecting boxes labeled with short hand-drawn symbols for goals, steps, and schedule, with arrows and white space.

scenes.narration: The sample came from a medium sized German university, with students from different faculties invited through boards, newsletters, and seminars.
scenes.layout_description: A campus notice board and small classroom doorway frame the invitation scene.
scenes.visual_prompt: A notice board, newsletter sheet, and seminar room doorway with tiny student figures entering; minimalist campus feel.

scenes.narration: Participants received no incentives, and all points of measurement happened within the same semester context to avoid outside changes.
scenes.layout_description: A calendar and a closed loop arrow show the measurements staying within one semester.
scenes.visual_prompt: Calendar pages with three marked dates inside a circular arrow, plus a small crossed-out gift icon to show no incentives.

scenes.narration: The final analyzed group had a mean age of 23.30 years, and about half were female, with students from several subjects.
scenes.layout_description: A cluster of simple student figures is centered around a small age tag.
scenes.visual_prompt: A group of diverse student silhouettes with a hand-lettered age note and a small half-filled circle for female proportion.

scenes.narration: Before training, most students reported no or little experience with time management strategies, which the authors later treat as important.
scenes.layout_description: Two stacked bars dominate the slide, showing low experience categories as the largest shapes.
scenes.visual_prompt: Simple bar-like shapes with labels for no experience and little experience emphasized in orange, plus a small student thinking icon.

scenes.narration: Time management behaviour was measured with eighteen items, perceived stress with the tension scale, perceived control of time with ten items, and demands with five items.
scenes.layout_description: Four measurement cards are lined up, each with a tiny icon and item count.
scenes.visual_prompt: Four clipboard cards with small checkboxes and hand-lettered counts, one card highlighted for tension, all in minimalist line art.

scenes.narration: At time one, time management behaviour related positively to perceived control of time, while stress and demands showed a strong negative and positive link.
scenes.layout_description: A simple correlation web uses arrows and small plus or minus marks between four circles.
scenes.visual_prompt: Four connected circles with arrows and tiny plus/minus symbols, using orange to highlight the link between control and stress.

scenes.narration: After training, reported use of the taught strategies increased significantly by four weeks, and the two week increase was nearly significant.
scenes.layout_description: A rising line climbs from the first to third measurement, with the middle point marked as almost there.
scenes.visual_prompt: A simple upward line graph with three points, the last point circled in orange, and the middle point marked with a dotted highlight.

scenes.narration: For the main outcomes, the repeated measures analysis showed a significant overall time effect and a significant stress effect after two weeks.
scenes.layout_description: Two outcome cards sit under a bold arrow from pretest to posttest one.
scenes.visual_prompt: A pretest-to-posttest arrow over two cards, one for stress with a downward arrow and one for control with a faint upward hint.

scenes.narration: Two weeks after training, students reported significantly less stress, while perceived control of time only showed a tendency in the expected direction.
scenes.layout_description: A downward stress arrow is bold, while the control arrow is lighter and dotted.
scenes.visual_prompt: A student figure with a heavy downward orange arrow beside stress and a faint upward dotted arrow beside control of time.

scenes.narration: Four weeks after training, both outcomes changed significantly: perceived stress was lower and perceived control of time was higher.
scenes.layout_description: Two bold arrows point in opposite directions from the same student figure.
scenes.visual_prompt: A split scene with a downward arrow labeled stress and an upward arrow labeled control, both in orange and yellow accents.

scenes.narration: The control variable, demands, did not change significantly at either follow up, which supports the authors' interpretation of a training effect.
scenes.layout_description: A steady horizontal line sits under the two follow up points, contrasting with changing outcome lines.
scenes.visual_prompt: A flat line for demands across three time points, with the other measures shown as changing curves nearby.

scenes.narration: Students with no or little prior experience seemed to benefit more than those with moderate or some experience, especially for perceived stress.
scenes.layout_description: Two small student groups are shown, one with a larger highlight around it.
scenes.visual_prompt: Two clusters of students, one surrounded by a brighter orange halo and one smaller, both near a training icon.

scenes.narration: The authors suggest that prioritizing, goal setting, daily planning, and monitoring may give students more orientation and help reduce stress.
scenes.layout_description: A path with signposts leads from confusion to a clearer route.
scenes.visual_prompt: A student walking along a simple path with signposts labeled by icons for goals, planning, and checkmarks, moving toward a calmer area.

scenes.narration: They also argue that daily planning may help start goal directed behaviour, and monitoring may provide reinforcing information about completed tasks.
scenes.layout_description: A checklist fills up from empty to checked, with a small spark of emphasis beside it.
scenes.visual_prompt: Checklist page with several boxes turning into checkmarks, plus a small orange sparkle around the completed items.

scenes.narration: The study is preliminary because the sample was small, and the authors say larger student samples are needed for more robust conclusions.
scenes.layout_description: A tiny group of students stands beside a much larger empty outline group.
scenes.visual_prompt: Small cluster of students next to a larger ghosted outline of a group, emphasizing limited sample size.

scenes.narration: About half the students left before the second measurement, although the authors note that such dropout rates are common in similar studies.
scenes.layout_description: A line of students splits, with some figures fading out after the first checkpoint.
scenes.visual_prompt: A simple participant flow showing a group shrinking between checkpoints, with faded figures leaving the path.

scenes.narration: The authors also say future studies should compare time management training with other stress reducing interventions and examine whether effects persist.
scenes.layout_description: Two different intervention paths branch away from the same starting point.
scenes.visual_prompt: A forked path with one branch labeled training and another branch with a different stress intervention icon, both leading forward.

scenes.narration: They mention possible practical advice for students: prioritize tasks, set clear goals with deadlines, plan the work day, and monitor progress.
scenes.layout_description: A neat student planner fills the center, surrounded by four small action icons.
scenes.visual_prompt: Open planner with small icons for priority list, target, calendar deadline, and checkmark progress, all hand-drawn.

scenes.narration: The authors suggest these ideas could be taught in higher education, for example to freshmen or in courses with long projects.
scenes.layout_description: A classroom scene shows a teacher pointing to a project board and a first year student nearby.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal classroom with a board showing a long project timeline, a freshman figure, and a teacher pointing with an orange marker.

scenes.narration: Overall, the paper concludes that time management training might help undergraduate well-being by reducing perceived stress and increasing perceived control of time.
scenes.layout_description: The final slide brings the two main outcomes together around a calm student figure.
scenes.visual_prompt: A calm student centered between a lowered stress symbol and a raised control symbol, with subtle orange and yellow highlights.

scenes.narration: The takeaway is cautious but useful: time management training showed promising effects here, yet the authors call for more student intervention studies.
scenes.layout_description: A closing banner sits above a small stack of research papers and a student icon.
scenes.visual_prompt: A simple closing scene with a stack of papers, a student silhouette, and a small upward arrow suggesting future research.
